subject: Veridian: tiered log snapshot & targeted erase process (evidence request)
messages:
From: Sarah Blake <sarah.blake@veridianhealth.com>

Cc: Compliance Ops <compliance@veridianhealth.com>, Jake Mills <jake.mills@veridianhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: customer-specific retention carveout and evidence for ephemeral logs

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, Veridian is requesting a short-term carveout to retain a scoped set of session logs for 90 days (instead of our standard 30d ephemeral window) for a specific tenant used in a pilot. The SOC 2 audit team needs:

- A short narrative explaining the justification for the 90d window (business reason + compensating controls)
- Exact log types retained (session traces, request metadata, anonymized prompt/response hashes)
- Evidence that logs for other tenants remain on the 30d cadence
- A signed, customer-specific exception form we can include in our audit binder

Can you share an evidence bundle and the approval path? Also confirm where the evidence will be stored (we prefer an internal drive link + a signed DocuSign).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — auditor deadline is 2027-05-03.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Blake
Sr. InfoSec Manager, Veridian Health

--
Veridian — Confidential

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Blake <sarah.blake@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: customer-specific retention carveout and evidence for ephemeral logs

Hi Sarah — thanks for laying this out. We can support the 90d scoped retention for the pilot tenant with the following approach:

1) Scope: tenant-id T-VER-PILOT only; retained artifacts limited to session indices, request/response md5 hashes, and routing metadata (no full user text).
2) Controls: access limited to a named ops account, audit logging enabled for all access, and read-only export capability.
3) Segregation: retained snapshots stored in an encrypted, tenant-tagged bucket with lifecycle policy and an immutable manifest.
4) Evidence: we will produce an evidence bundle with retention config, ACL screenshots, export logs, and a sampled CSV demonstrating TTL enforcement for other tenants.

I will assemble the packet and route for internal approval (security + product). Ben, can you coordinate the log sample and include the exact S3 object paths? Marissa, will legal need to sign a customer exception form or can we use our standard exception template?

Targeting a packet back to Veridian by 2027-04-29 to give you time before the auditor review.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Security Lead | Redwood Inference
